final.title: When rounding becomes a workflow problem
final.body:
If you keep “rounding claims” as a vague complaint, it stays hard to automate and easy to argue about. I’d turn it into one bounded workflow decision: where do small numerical gaps actually change what you do?

Start with one recurring workflow you already handle in digital documents or SaaS tools. It might be invoice rounding, currency conversion, timesheet variance, or an estimate-to-actual gap. The point is not the label; it is the moment where two slightly different numbers force someone to decide whether the gap matters.

Then draw the control boundary. Which cases are already policy, like rounding to the nearest cent? Which need human judgment, like flagging a gap above your own threshold? Which still have no rule at all? If the difference is invisible and acceptable, it can stay in the background. If it is visible and affects approval or audit notes, it needs a clear human step.

The next practical step is to write one rule in plain English for one workflow. For example: “round amounts to the nearest cent; flag any gap above my threshold for review before I approve the invoice.” Then ask yourself one diagnostic question: do I already document why I accepted the difference, or do I just let it pass? If you cannot write the rule clearly yet, fix the policy first. The machine can wait; paperwork rarely does.
